nodes.label: Module 11 — Orders (clinical-order spine)
nodes.rationale: Every non-medication clinical intervention flows through a single authenticated auditable order; M11 also owns the signature primitive that M12 and any future order-producing module consume.

nodes.label: order_record Spine + per-kind TypeBox data jsonb (D1)
nodes.rationale: Adding a kind is a per-kind TypeBox sub-PR, never an ALTER TABLE; CMS revises CoP 418.104/106 interpretations periodically and the per-kind TypeBox absorbs the churn.

nodes.label: Seven-State XState Order Lifecycle Machine (D2)
nodes.rationale: XState gives compile-time exhaustiveness — every transition named, every guard typed, every side effect in one place. Ad-hoc booleans like is_signed/is_discontinued drift and produce illegal combinations; a five-state model without verbal_pending and expired_unsigned loses the CMS 418.104(b) compliance signal.

nodes.label: 48-Hour Verbal-Order Window, Platform Floor Tenant-Tighten-Only (D3)
nodes.rationale: CMS sets 'reasonable time'; industry and most state-board codifications land at 48 hours with stricter state rules common. The platform floor protects tenants from configuring an unsafe-from-survey window while allowing tightening to as short as 1 hour; auto-detecting state from patient address was rejected as too fragile for travelling clinicians.

nodes.label: Polymorphic OrderSignatureProvider Seam (target_kind discriminator, D4)
nodes.rationale: A polymorphic FK in PostgreSQL is messy, so integrity is enforced at the application layer through the typed seam. M11 owns the signature primitive, verbal timer and cosign workflow once; M12 consumes without M11 importing M12 — avoiding a dependency-graph cycle.

nodes.label: Standing-Order Template + Spawned-Instance Engine (D5)
nodes.rationale: Standing orders in hospice are signature-anchored — the medical director signs the template and spawns inherit the signature per CMS interpretation; re-signing each spawn would generate clinician fatigue and contradict the regulatory reading. Per ADR-0019 D2 the spawner runs only against an authorized prescriber's signed protocol, carrying the authorizing-protocol reference and prescriber identity.

nodes.label: Discontinuation as Command + Cascade with Its Own Row (D13)
nodes.rationale: The discontinuation row is the audit anchor preserving actor, reason, effective time and cascade attribution — a bare status flip loses all of it and turns 'show me everything discontinued for adverse event last quarter' into an unqueryable audit-event scan. Mirrors M6's revocation/discharge command+cascade.

nodes.label: Orthogonal Lab Transmission & Results Lifecycle (D16, D17, D18, D19)
nodes.rationale: Transmission retry is M29-owned and M11 only observes, because duplicating the backoff loop would double-execute. Result attachment does NOT auto-complete the order — 42 CFR 418.106 requires documented clinician review of significant findings, so the active→completed transition stays a clinician decision. The lab-observation back-reference is a single latest-pointer UUID with no cross-module FK; full history stays in M29's authoritative link table.

nodes.label: OrderProvider Seam (getOrdersSince / findActiveOrder / timeliness)
nodes.rationale: Lets M11 ship today and M12/M14/M21/M23/M28/M30/M33 attach when they lock; the dependency-cruiser boundary check enforces that consumers may not import M11's Drizzle schema, only the seam types.

nodes.label: Assessment-Trigger Banner as Derived Valkey Projection (D7)
nodes.rationale: Storing a suggestion as a first-class entity invites auto-approve and bulk-approve workflows that bypass clinical judgement; the derived TTL-bounded projection keeps M9/M10 as the source of truth while the order's triggering_*_id preserves the audit trail.

nodes.label: LOC-Change and Recertification Orders Are Advisory (D9, D10)
nodes.rationale: M6 is the source of truth for LOC and benefit-period state with its billing and IPU implications; M11 authorizes the change and M6 executes it. Two modules touching the same table would race, and M11 enforcing the F2F window would duplicate M6's window scanner.

nodes.label: EPCS Explicitly Out of Scope for M11 (D15)
nodes.rationale: EPCS is a federal regime distinct from the general CMS clinical-record signature requirement; conflating them would force every M11 signature to clear an EPCS bar that does not apply to labs, DME or supplies. M12 wraps M11's primitive with the DEA identity proofing.

nodes.label: Per-Tenant withOrgContext Sweep Replacing Cross-Tenant Platform Scan (M11-F03)
nodes.rationale: The lab-results-overdue sweep no longer runs a cross-tenant PHI scan under withPlatformContext with no org predicate; it enumerates active org ids (non-PHI) and processes each tenant under its own withOrgContext so RLS scopes every read and write.

nodes.label: Outbox-Only Cross-Module Communication Rule (D6, D8)
nodes.rationale: Outbox publication is the only cross-module communication M11 performs; it never calls another module's HTTP route. Direct HTTP between domain modules introduces fan-out, latency variance and partial-failure modes, whereas outbox plus idempotency dedup gives at-least-once delivery with deterministic side effects. Polling another module's tables would be a schema-import violation and a retrograde dependency.
